summary: All fourteen bodies read, including four complete shader stages, both full studies, renderer, recorder and abbreviated integration excerpts. Keep explicit graph setup, captured renderer/study ownership and finally cleanup. Revise raw shader reads, controls that duplicate their own initial values, and cube-shader readability. A fixed fragment camera position disagrees with the orbiting vertex camera and needs runtime confirmation.

lenses.smells_idioms: owner captures the inherited Renderer for frames work; owned captures this run's lab so old finalizers cannot close the newly published property. Both captures are justified and are not redundant box aliases. The raw local lab read only closes a prior local instance without resolving an ancestor; retain this narrowly scoped escape until equivalent local optional lookup/lifecycle ownership is demonstrated. Raw vertex/fragment reads have an existing typed nullable inherited API and need no escape hatch.
lenses.imports: Inspected results-reconciled.jsonl for all occurrences. Renderer drops redundant Rect but retains Options; recorder drops unused OpenDlssNrStudy but retains Path/createDirectories; image-study keeps its OpenDlssNrStudy import; integration retains neural.*. Full ink/cube studies are parse-review at :::fold, so imports including neural.* have no removal verdict. Coordinator must extract directives before analyzer; stars remain without resolution evidence.
lenses.whitespace: Kotlin control blocks compress assignments, bounds and callbacks onto single lines; mechanical formatting can expose them after fold extraction. GLSL objectPoint/project/main combine multiple geometric steps on one line, so the teaching edit should name camera basis and face points as well as expand layout. Preserve cube triangle index data as rows of triangles/faces rather than arbitrary formatter wrapping.
lenses.comments: Ink comments explain fixed grain, loops, charcoal echoes and linear output. Cube Scene push members and world-to-clip camera basis need local units/mode explanations because the shader is intended to be edited. Existing prose establishes source/NR/grade ordering and recording ownership. Add why prior local lab and owned captures remain instead of mechanically removing them.
lenses.glsl: Read vertex and fragment interfaces together: matching locations 0..4, world-space positions/normals and clip positions, fullscreen top-left UV, Study.frame time/size, linearized ink output. Cube view-dependent specular uses a fixed camera while project() orbits its actual camera; flag separately as suspected behavior. NR gets color only; nowClip/oldClip are not motion input to this study and must not be presented as temporal reconstruction.
lenses.live_coding: Keep fold/endfold directives and all existing fragment markers (none of the fourteen bodies contains //%-). Controls are mutable captures and shader reload occurs in frames; do not hoist shader text into immutable snapshots that would stop observing edits. Preserve invalid-reload fallback, finally cleanup and recording guard. Control initialValue literals should follow their named vars to support one-place edits.
lenses.helpers: Checked Already in Field/Approved/Declined. Existing vertex/fragment properties, OpenDlssNrStudy, reload and saveFrame already provide the reusable operations. Do not propose declined automatic pass-chain attachment or fabricate default imports. A general control-panel API is not justified by two intentionally complete listings until ownership/recording contracts are settled; no new helper proposed.

findings.issue: Style, tone, structure, intensity, animate and RGB defaults are separately hardcoded in variables and widget initial values in both study bodies. Changing a named creative value can leave the displayed control reporting the old value.
findings.proposed_change: Initialize controls from the corresponding variable (for example initialValue = style.toDouble(), initialValue = red.toDouble(), initialValue = animate) and keep the named vars together above the panel. Preserve the defaults and recording behavior.
findings.verification: Change one named style/grade/animation default, rerun, and verify both widget state and GPU output agree; confirm unchanged defaults reproduce the reference.

findings.issue: Fragment specular computes the world-space view vector from fixed eye (5,3.7,5), while vertex project() at 168-170 orbits eye with t*.18 when settings.y == 1. OpenDlssNrStudy.render sets settings.y to 1, so these cameras diverge after time zero. This is a source-derived suspected lighting defect, not a tested visual failure.
findings.proposed_change: Use the actual orbiting world-space eye in the fragment half vector, sharing the camera position calculation or passing eye as a stage varying. Keep lighting and projection spaces explicit.
findings.verification: On the real GPU, compare highlights during a controlled camera orbit with fixed object/light state, then rerun the cube clip and confirm SOURCE/NR/GRADE remain synchronized. No behavior claim can be closed by formatting alone.

findings.issue: The world-to-camera basis, view-depth projection and transformed triangle vertices are densely packed; readers changing the camera have to infer coordinate spaces and Vulkan depth convention across one-line expressions. The Scene vec4 packing is also only partially described outside the shader.
findings.proposed_change: Expand project() into named forward/right/up/view-offset/depth steps; comment Scene member units and settings flags using the producer assignments in OpenDlssNrStudy.render. Group main() into background triangle, object/face geometry and projection, preserving all equations and the Vulkan depth mapping.
findings.verification: Compile the vertex/fragment pair, compare push offsets and stage interfaces, and inspect the same-frame source capture for unchanged geometry when only layout/comments change.
